title: Modi Heads to Manila for ASEAN-India and East Asia Summits
excerpt: Maritime cooperation and the $122 billion trade relationship lead the agenda on November 17, with an AITIGA review push — and no confirmed Quad or Trump meeting, the MEA says.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi travels to Manila on November 16 for the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit, with both leaders' meetings held on November 17.
  • Maritime security, regional stability and trade top the agenda; India is pushing for an early conclusion of the review of the ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA).
  • India-ASEAN trade stands at around $122 billion, and 2026 is the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation.
  • Modi said he looks forward to interacting with the Indian community in the Philippines during the visit; the MEA has not confirmed any Quad leaders' meeting or a meeting with US President Donald Trump on the sidelines.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will travel to Manila on Monday, November 16, to attend the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit, the Ministry of External Affairs has said. Maritime security, regional stability and expanding trade ties are expected to be the key focus areas of the visit, which runs to November 18.

"Will be in Manila, Philippines later today and tomorrow to attend the following programmes: 23rd Asean-India Summit. 21st East Asia Summit," Modi posted on X. "India attaches immense importance to close friendship with Asean nations. I'm also looking forward to interacting with the Indian community based in the Philippines," he added.

The Philippines, which chairs the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations this year, is hosting both summits. According to the MEA, Modi will attend a dinner hosted by Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr on November 16, then take part in the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit process on November 17. Bilateral meetings with other leaders are also being planned.

Maritime cooperation leads the agenda

India and ASEAN have marked 2026 as the Year of Maritime Cooperation, and maritime issues are expected to feature prominently, as the two sides share adjoining maritime zones and face common regional security challenges. Speaking at a special briefing, MEA Secretary (East) Rudrendra Tandon said India's engagement with ASEAN — as a grouping and with individual member countries — is an important part of its Act East policy. "We strongly believe that as an Indian Ocean country that abuts this very important Southeast Asian maritime zone, a strong strategic relationship with the Asean member states, as a collective as well as individually, is good for both of us," Tandon said.

The ASEAN-India Summit will review progress in implementing the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, including the ASEAN-India Plan of Action 2026–2030, and chart the future direction of cooperation, the MEA said. The East Asia Summit, an ASEAN-led forum that brings in regional and major global powers, is being held under the theme "Navigating the Future," with leaders expected to focus on strengthening cooperation and building resilience amid global uncertainties.

Trade: $122 billion and a stalled agreement review

Two-way trade between India and the bloc stands at around $122 billion, making ASEAN one of India's major trading partners. India is pushing for an early conclusion of the ongoing review of the India-ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA), which New Delhi hopes will help address trade imbalances and improve market access. Tandon said discussions on the review were continuing, while acknowledging that negotiations involving multiple countries take time.

Defence ties and regional questions

The host country is itself a defence partner: the Philippines became India's first foreign customer for the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile in 2022, signing a $375-million deal for three shore-based anti-ship missile batteries, and Philippine defence secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr recently indicated Manila was interested in additional systems and had submitted a wish list to India. On the South China Sea, India has maintained that any ASEAN-China Code of Conduct should be consistent with international law, particularly the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. Myanmar is also likely to feature in regional discussions; India has opposed diplomatic isolation of Myanmar, citing its 1,643-km shared border and connectivity projects including the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project, and Myanmar is expected to be represented in Manila by a foreign ministry official.

The unconfirmed meeting

The visit has drawn attention amid discussion of a possible Quad leaders' summit involving India, the US, Japan and Australia. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio had indicated last month that the Quad summit was planned alongside the wider meetings in the Philippines. The MEA, however, said it had no confirmed information on such a meeting or on a possible interaction between Modi and US President Donald Trump. Any Modi-Trump meeting, if scheduled, would come amid ongoing India-US trade negotiations.
